core_meaning.short_meaning: Judge, arbiter, one who decides justly
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Hakem corresponds to the Arabic form حاكم (Arabic root ح ك م (ḥ-k-m); حَاكِم (Ḥākim)). Its core sense is judge, arbiter, one who decides justly. Hakem is Arabic حَاكِم (Ḥākim) 'judge, ruler, one who decides', the active participle of the root ح ك م (ḥ-k-m) 'to judge, to rule'. The source gloss 'judge, arbiter, ruler' is correct. The source's claim that the name is 'one of the beautiful names of Allah' is imprecise: the divine name is الحَكَم / الحَاكِم, and the personal name is a separate usage. The source's historical references (Al-Hakim bi-Amr Allah, 'Al-Hakim II') and its 'Ibrahim Hakem of Riyadh' story were fabricated and are not carried over.
